title: Applications of primary decomposition: diagonalizable plus nilpotent parts
objectives: Solve linear initial value problems with generalized eigenvector chains
Prove existence and uniqueness of the diagonalizable-plus-nilpotent splitting
Prove the cyclic decomposition for a prime-power minimal polynomial
Compute Jordan and rational canonical forms
prerequisites: The primary decomposition theorem (Chapter 19), diagonalizability and direct sums (Chapters 16 to 18).
source_scope: The captions of the three recordings (positions 40 to 42) were read in full. The 2 by 2 system and the six- and eight-dimensional examples follow them; the running matrix is from Chapter 12; the proofs of the canonical-form theorems, the laboratory and the exercises are original.
